adc_input.basis: Measured: the twelve key-row values seg5 0xc8ce9c keeps at 0xfdb018, read over the live service in REC after a normal power-on with all keys released (X-T20 2.11, 2026-10-29), assigned to channels 0-11 in order (the xpro-lab emulator model). Channel 3 is the ladder for the 4-way pad, OK, Q and DISP/BACK; channel 2 carries the S1/S2 thresholds 0x28/0x1d0. Channels 0, 1, 7, 8, 10 and 11 vary between power-ons. The channel order and the values of channels 10 and 11 are not confirmed against the converter registers.

gpio_input.basis: Measured: the sixteen GPIO input words X-T20 2.11 stage 2 snapshots into the boot information (+0x00), read over the live service after a normal SD-boot power-on without a cable (2026-10-29): shutter released, VBUS (bank 1 bit 14) low, lens attached, card inserted. A second normal power-on (2026-10-22) differs only in bank 1 bits 3/5. With VBUS high the start mode becomes JIG. Pin roles from seg5 key rows (table 0xec6e10): bank 0 bit 11 LENS_DET and bank 10 bit 4 CARD_DET active low.

pll_input.basis: Firmware: the kernel entry bypasses stage 2, whose PLL table 0xe0e8 (X-T20 2.11) powers PLL 0 and 3 up (clear bits 27:26, set bit 26, wait for the lock at 0xfff0b06c; 0x7e64), powers PLL 2 down (bit 27) and leaves PLL 1 and 4 at reset. Section 5 later re-enables PLL 0 by setting only bit 26 (0xc6aa74), which assumes it is powered. The reset values of PLL 1 and 4 are not measured.

sd_card.basis: Declared, not measured: an empty 8 GiB SDHC card with high speed and without UHS-I or UHS-II modes, formatted as one FAT32 partition from sector 8192 with 32 KiB clusters, the layout of the other FujiMod REC configurations. A card was inserted during the measured power-ons (bank 10 bit 4 CARD_DET low); its identity, size and contents are not read.

i2c_parts.basis: Touch-panel controller at 0x01 on bus 1 (device 13 of the X-T20 2.11 I2C descriptor table 0xed412c), driven only by the touchPanel task (mailbox 0x4a, entry 0xc9aff4, created by 0xc9b7a8). Start-up selects page 0x3e or 0x3f through register 0xff (0xc9ac8c) and writes registers 0x3e11, 0x3e12 and 0x3fdc. The task reads a touch report (ten bytes from register 0x3f00 through 0xc9af8c) only on its event bit 0x10 (0xc9b208); the strict REC and menu runs never take that path, which would stop on an undeclared register read. Presence is declared, not measured, and no registers are declared.

Part at 0x1b on bus 1 (device 12). Start-up 0xceb630 writes register 0 with configuration byte 0x3d7; nothing is read before REC. Its identity is not established; presence is declared, not measured, and no registers are declared.

Three-axis accelerometer at 0x1c on bus 1 (device 8). 0xc7a6e0 writes the configuration table (register 0x2a = 0x65 last) and 0xc7a77c reads six bytes from register 1 as 12-bit left-justified big-endian X, Y and Z. The values are the median of the five samples in the rings at 0xfdad50 + 0x46/0x5a/0x6e of the s1 REC capture (2026-10-29): X -1024, Y 26, Z -92 counts; s2 and s3 agree within 3 counts.

Eye-sensor proximity part at 0x39 on bus 1 (device 4). Its command byte is 0xa0 | address (0xc76484). Start-up writes the thresholds and ENABLE = 0x2f; 0xc76500 reads STATUS 0x13 (bit 5: proximity interrupt) and the count at 0x18/0x19, low byte first. The s1-s3 captures hold eye state 2 (no eye, 0xfdad40) with a far-to-near threshold of 662. The declared count 0 is below that threshold and the status has no interrupt pending; neither value is measured.

dram_refresh.basis: Measured: X-T20 2.11 0xc8f09c caches the refresh-rate level from bits 8..10 of DRAM controller +0xec at 0xfdbea8 + 5; the s1, s2 and s3 REC captures (2026-10-29) hold level 2 there, with refresh word 0xc30 at 0xfdbea8 and no second controller (0xfda438 = 0).

execution_clock.basis: Estimated from camera timing: the marker log read over the live service on 2026-10-22 (a REC re-entry) times step 0x02010100 at 0.182 ms and step 0x02040100 at 0.128 ms (medians of 2 and 3); the strict REC run executes 36082 and 24216 instructions in them, about 198 and 189 million instructions per second, or 4 per 48 MHz tick. Both steps send messages and set state without waiting for hardware; steps with waits give lower rates (0x02010200 141, 0x02010500 139, live-view frames 147 million per second) and 0x02010300, whose busy-wait costs instructions in proportion to the clock, a higher one. Without a declared clock each core executes one instruction per tick, about 20 times fewer than the xpro-lab model's 1 ns per instruction.

lens.basis: The lens of the s1, s2 and s3 REC captures (2026-10-29) and of the 2026-10-22 live-view dump: its information page with synthetic serial 00A0000, based on the layout the body keeps at 0x11e3958 ("LY043A", "FLSNW039AF 25/1.7 XF") and the replies of the link history 0x11d542c (commands 0x20 -> 0x300 and 0x26 -> 0x1c, the only commands of 90 s of idle traffic recorded on 2026-10-22); start-up commands are not recorded and are answered with 0. Wiring from X-T20 2.11 section 5: link on serial channel 0 (0xfff28000, resource 0xe); lswatch checks the contacts bank 14 bits 0/1 high and bank 11 bits 0/1/2 high/low/high, then switches bank 14 register 1 bit 0 high; the ready ISRs 0xc7b36c / 0xc7b338 sample bank 14 bit 1 after interrupt 166 (rows 0x52/0x53 of 0xed471c; 0xc5cfd4 maps it to external line 15). The delays (20 ms to the ready signal, 200 ms of initialization, 60 ms per focus drive) and the 1 ms power sampling are assumptions from the xpro-lab lens model, not measurements; the camera's lens step 0x01091300 takes about 86 ms. The body's stored records for the lens are in `registration`.

registration.basis: Synthetic registered-lens list at flash 0x3820000: an eight-byte header with signature 0xabc123f9, head/tail index 0 and one 0x80-byte entry at index 0. The entry has short display name AF 25/1., lens name FLSNW039, serial 00A0000, lens version bytes 01 05 and body version bytes 01 46. Previous/next indices are 0xff; all other entry fields are zero. Correction storage is left erased. Placed with the user profile only.

shutter.basis: Shutter of X-T20 2.11. imgdc (section 6 0x17d3800..0x17d4600) arms one sensor's external interrupt source through 0xd09c3c (source 32 from 0x17d3b50 with line 3 inverted, 0xfff0a008 <- 0x8000b; source 31 from 0x17d3b98 with line 3 not inverted, <- 0x80003; rows 0xf67188 and resources 0x55/0x56 give GIC 154, which the distributor configures edge triggered: ICFGR 0xffff1c24 <- 0xa80000), drives the motor (0x17fbc54(1, ..): bank 1 +0x0c <- 0x30001 then 0xc0000, pin 0 in mode 1, pin 1 in mode 0) and waits up to 100 ms for the interrupt, then brakes (0x17fbc54(2, 0)). The sensors are the sources' inputs in table 0xf67220: 31 = bank 0 bit 3, 32 = bank 10 bit 2. At the end of a sequence 0x17c46ec wants both high (and source 33, bank 15 bit 1, low); otherwise imgdc reports an error that re-initializes REC (flags 0x11d0843/0x11d0844, both 0 in the s1 capture). The power-on GPIO words hold 31 low and 32 high, and the boot runs a wait on 32, then one on 31. The positions (31, 32) = (0, 1), (0, 0), (1, 1) and the 30 ms step are inferred from those checks (xpro-lab ShutterMotor), not measured; the 1 ms sampling of the motor modes is a model choice. Each step gives line 3 one edge.

loader_handoff.basis: Camera capture: the 0x5c0-byte stage-2 block the kernel copies to 0x7f4fc, read over the resident live service in REC after a normal SD-boot power-on without a cable (X-T20 2.11, 2026-10-29; block SHA-256 ab399d185a974beeee3ce66c91e64c74b02d1b9f9800d7c0309ed0ebea0a7fad, ram_low SHA-256 3065c7420bc1cad0edb97504e6715e38d1e0a3b2db791e7f7eef626f07146430). +0x00 holds the 16 power-on GPIO input words, +0x140 the sub-CPU power-on cause 0x12 and +0x188 the stage-2 ADC words. Placed in a free RAM gap; kernel entry bypasses the boot ROM and stage 2.

flash_aperture.basis: Declared discovery input: the update image from its flash offset; bytes past it read erased, including the configuration store at flash 0x3840000, which the firmware then rebuilds from its defaults.

nor.basis: Declared discovery input. The X-T20 2.11 driver addresses chip select 0 below aperture 0xf4000000 (0xc505dc) and uses 4 KiB (0x21), 64 KiB (0xdc) erase and 256-byte 4PP (0x12) page programs (command table 0xed3f9c). The chip part, its reset configuration and all latencies are not measured; the ticks are synthetic.

battery_gauge.basis: Measured: the battery task of X-T20 2.11 keeps the gauge's replies in its block at 0xfda4fc (status register 0 at +0, register 8 at +4, 0x0c at +6, 0x10 at +8; 0xc711f0..0xc712bc), read over the live service in the s1 REC capture (2026-10-29). The s2 and s3 captures and the 2026-10-22 live-view dumps agree on register 0 and register 8 (0); register 0x0c ranges over 0x1cb..0x202 and 0x10 over 0x2b6..0x2bf. Wiring from section 5: the gauge sits on serial port 4 (resource 0xf of 0xed389c, chip select bank 13 bit 8, 8-bit transfers). 0xc70748 sends register << 16 | value as three bytes inside one enabled transfer (+0x08 written 1 by 0xc4b87c and 0 by 0xc4b8c0); the first byte names the register and bit 0 writes it, and the bytes read back from +0x60 carry the value, high byte first. The start-up 0xc70e7c polls register 0 until bit 15 is set and then writes 0x405 to register 0x60. Unlisted registers read zero, including 0x1c and the updater's 0x54; they are not measured. Register 0x54 is the data-line detection: after a cable raises VBUS, the USB manager 0x168ece0 writes 0xb00 to register 0x50 and reads 0x54, and (value & 0xd) == 1 means a PC, anything else a charger. It is declared 1, so a cable always reaches a PC; the camera's value is not measured.

usb_cable.basis: Declared input. VBUS of the USB port is GPIO bank 1 pin 14 (0xc4e138(0x1000e), 0x1527d94), 1 = cable: the USB driver task polls it every 25 ms (message 0x1433, 0x152e334) and after 16 equal polls posts 0x142f (connected) or 0x1430 (removed) through 0x152d82c. The X-T20's Micro-B port is USB 2.0, so a host negotiates high speed; the driver also programs DCFG for high speed (0x20000).

clock.basis: Declared input. The sub-CPU keeps the calendar as seconds since 2000-01-01 00:00 in registers 0x41..0x44 (register-table rows 9..12 of 0xed6a0c), least significant byte first: 0xc70058 reads the four bytes until the low byte reads the same twice, and 0xc75800 converts the count (0xce7230). 0xc700c0 sets the clock: it writes 0 to register 0x45 (row 13), the four bytes, 1 to 0x45 and 0 to 0x46. No code reads 0x45, so it is taken as the run/hold control. The count is not measured on the camera; 846555480 is 2026-10-29 02:18, the local time of the s1 reference capture. Device time runs at 48 MHz.

sub_cpu.basis: Declared discovery input. Segment 5 reaches the sub-CPU through 16-bit words on serial port 2 (0xc6fb10, 0xc6fbb4; register table 0xed6a0c): bits 14..8 name the register, bit 15 writes the low byte, and the word read back from +0x60 (0xc4b964) carries the register value. Register 0x60 is the power-on cause; 0x10 is the normal start the camera reported (loader handoff word power_on_cause). Registers 0x50-0x5f hold the 16-byte settings header that 0xcdd670 validates; a selected user profile places its header there (profile_header); otherwise they read zero, so the firmware loads its defaults and writes the stock header back. Unlisted registers read zero; the register file is not measured beyond these reads.
